nodes.name: Pt SA impregnation on WO_{3-x}/WO_3
nodes.procedure: The WO_{3-x} or WO_3 (0.3 g) was dispersed in 25 mL ultrapure water by sonicated for 10 min and then an appropriate amount of H_2PtCl_6, 6H2O (2 mg mL^{-1}) was added dropwise into the solution, followed by stirring at 70 °C (343 K) for 4 h. The obtained product was separated by centrifugation and washed with ultrapure water and anhydrous ethanol thoroughly. After drying [60 °C (333 K), in vacuum, 12 h] and further calcination [300 °C (573 K), in air, 4 h], the Pt SA-WO_{3-x} and Pt SA-WO_3 were obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms Pt single atoms (brighter spots) dispersed on WO3-x nanosheet surface; intensity profile shows Pt higher than surrounding W atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field-scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping profiles confirm that the Pt single atoms (marked by the orange circles) are dispersed on the surface of WO3-x nanosheet (Fig. 1A and SI Appendix, Fig. S6). The intensity profile taken along the orange line in SI Appendix, Fig. S7 reveals that the intensity of the brighter spot ... was higher than that of the surrounding W atom column.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ TEM shows reversible lattice expansion mainly at outmost (020) layer of WO3-x support in Pt SA-WO3-x from 3.8 Å (Ar) → 3.9 Å (180s NO) → 4.1 Å (380s NO), reversible with Ar purge, under NO/H2=1:4 at 150°C; no change for WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Pt SA-WO3-x (Fig. 2A), the lattice fringes with a spacing of 3.8Å was assigned to a clean WO3-x (020) surface under Ar. After the 180 s of exposure to the input of NO, we directly observed the lattice fringe spacing of WO3-x expanded from 3.8Å to 3.9Å ... After 380s NO exposure, the surface lattice spacing of WO3-x was expanded to 4.1Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in situ AP-XPS of Pt SA-WO3-x shows Ptδ+ (75.43 eV, 72.03 eV) in UHV transforming during reaction at 150°C (NO:H2=1:4) to include Pt0 peaks (74.08 eV, 70.58 eV) indicating Pt cluster formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the ultra-high-vacuum (SI Appendix, Fig. S19A), the binding energies of 75.43 eV and 72.03 eV were assigned to the Ptδ+ (0<δ<2) in the Pt SA-WO3-x (26). While at reaction conditions (SI Appendix, Fig. S19B), we found that the Pt on Pt SA-WO3-x showed the decreased binding energies and additional peaks at 74.08 eV and 70.58 eV (assigned to the Pt0 species), indicating the formation of Pt clusters.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ CO adsorption DRIFTS shows linear CO on Ptδ+ at 2120 cm⁻¹ before reaction and redshift to 2106 cm⁻¹ after reaction for Pt SA-WO3-x, indicating Pt cluster formation; 2084 cm⁻¹ assigned to Pt nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The adsorption of CO bands centered at 2,120 cm⁻¹ was ascribed to linearly bonded CO on the top of Ptδ+ single-atom sites, and the peak at 2,084 cm⁻¹ was assigned to the adsorbed CO on Pt nanoparticles (SI Appendix, Fig. S18) (24, 25). It was noteworthy that the redshift of the IR peak from 2,120 cm⁻¹ to 2,106 cm⁻¹ after the reaction (Fig. 1E), indicates Pt clusters were formed during the reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of Pt SA-WO3-x under 2000 ppm NO/He at 150°C shows red shift of W-O-W peaks (815→809, 703→695, 328→325, 266→261 cm⁻¹) indicating W-O bond stretching; reversible after gas removal; no shift for Pt SA-WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for the Pt SA-WO3-x, all vibrational characteristic peaks (815 cm⁻¹, 703 cm⁻¹, 328 cm⁻¹, and 266 cm⁻¹) of W-O-W bonds showed a red shift (809 cm⁻¹, 695 cm⁻¹, 325 cm⁻¹, and 261 cm⁻¹) after the sample was exposed to NO for 30 min at 150°C (423 K) (Fig. 3B).

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-temperature programmed reduction reveals abundant surface oxygen vacancies on WO3-x compared to WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is also confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), electron paramagnetic resonance, H2-temperature program reduction, and O2-temperature program desorption results of WO3-x and WO3, which obviously reveal that the abundant surface oxygen vacancies exist on the WO3-x surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and FFT show crystal lattice of WO3 distorted in WO3-x due to oxygen defects; confirms Pt clusters <1 nm (green circles) after reaction for Pt SA-WO3-x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM and corresponding fast Fourier Transform (FFT) (Fig. 1 B and C) reveal that the crystal lattice of WO3 became distorted in the WO3-x due to the introduction of oxygen defects (19). Notably, Pt single atoms on the WO3-x were unstable and easily transformed into Pt clusters with diameters of <1 nm after reaction, confirmed by HAADF-STEM (Fig. 1D and SI Appendix, Fig. S15, marked by the green circles).
